description: We are slowly building India's next tech giant company that is Phoenix.Ai Let's build something out of this world .
summary:
Across India, the United States, and East Africa, farmers are dealing with erratic rain, hotter summers, falling groundwater, and tired soil. Still, most stick to familiar monocultures like Rice-Wheat in Lucknow, Alfalfa in Nevada, or Maize in Kenya because changing crops feels risky. Traditional satellite dashboards do not solve this because most smallholder farmers do not read complex GIS maps, and a coarse 9 km satellite pixel often misses what is actually happening on a 1-acre plot.

We built TerraShift to connect 23 NASA and partner Earth observation datasets directly to farmers in their own language. On the left side of our screen, a farmer can talk naturally with our voice assistant Raghav over a simulated 2G keypad phone call or WhatsApp in Hindi, Awadhi, English, or Swahili. On the right side, our agronomic math engine checks live 5-day weather for daily irrigation decisions, compares three crop rotations with real crop photos, solves the 60-day summer bare-soil heat problem, and warns when satellite data disagrees with local soil reality.
details:
1. Why We Built TerraShift & How It Works
Sitting here in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, we noticed a huge gap between space data and real farming. Every year between April and mid-June (right after wheat harvest and before paddy sowing), farm fields around us sit completely bare for nearly 60 days. Under 41.8C to 46C summer heat, the bare dirt bakes, soil organic carbon burns off, and deep moisture evaporates. At the same time, farmers keep repeating the same Rice-Wheat cycle in India, continuous Alfalfa in Nevada, or continuous Maize on steep slopes in Kenya.

Most teams try to solve this by building complicated GIS dashboards full of NDVI graphs. But a farmer standing in the sun with a basic 2G keypad phone or WhatsApp is never going to read a satellite raster.

So we built TerraShift using a Split-Brain design:

Left Side (The Farmer's World):
Farmers do not need to learn any map software. They can use our WhatsApp-style advisor or switch to our 2G Feature Phone simulator and press the green Call button. When they call, the phone rings and connects to "Raghav", our conversational agricultural assistant. Farmers can speak naturally in Hindi, Awadhi, English, or Swahili (or press keys 1 to 6) to ask about their soil texture (Retili/Sandy, Domat/Loam, or Chikni/Clay), white salt crusts (Usar), fertilizer costs, pest issues, or whether they should run their tube-well today. They can also upload a photo of their field soil, which our HTML5 Canvas scanner checks for bright surface crusting or dryness. Instead of scientific jargon, advice is given in spoken voice, real crop photographs, Water Buckets (for water saved), Fertilizer Bags (for free nitrogen fixed), and local currency (INR, USD, or KSh).

Right Side (The NASA Control Room & #BACKEND X-Ray):
For agricultural officers, researchers, and judges, the right panel runs four connected scientific modules:
- Live Weather & Smart Irrigation Advisor: Combines 5-day Open-Meteo rainfall forecasts with NASA SMAP soil moisture and FAO evapotranspiration (ET0) to answer the farmer's daily question: "Should I irrigate today or wait?" If rain (>=4 mm) is coming in 48 hours, it tells the farmer to hold irrigation, saving around Rs 1,800/ha in pump diesel.
- Module 1 (12-Month Bare-Soil & Heat Timeline): Maps monthly MODIS/Sentinel-2 NDVI against ECOSTRESS land surface temperature, highlighting the 60-day April-May bare-soil danger window and offering 6 practical summer solutions (60-Day Summer Moong 'Virat', 45-Day Dhaincha green manure, Bajra + Lobia cattle fodder, Summer Sesame/Maize, 21-Day Soil Solarization, or Zero-Water Wheat Stubble Mulch when water is below 20%).
- Module 2 (Interactive Sliders & 3-Way Rotation Cards): Lets users test water scarcity, El Nino drought shocks (-25% rain), farmer goals (cash, soil nitrogen, or fodder), and equipment (standard tractor vs. Zero-Till). It compares Option A (Baseline Monoculture), Option B (Water & Nitrogen-Saving Shift), and Option C (Saline/Sodic Soil Recovery) with real crop photograph sequences and all 5 challenge checkpoints (why suggested, NASA evidence, benefits, info gaps, and local review risks).
- Module 3 (The Truth Meter): A 9 km SMAP satellite pixel covers dozens of villages and canals, so it often says an area is moist even when a specific farmer's sandy plot is bone dry. Whenever field inputs or soil photos clash with the 9 km satellite signal, our Truth Meter fires a yellow/red alert, lowers the confidence score, and recommends a local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), USDA-NRCS, or KALRO lab test.
- Module 4 (Global Case Studies, Live GPS & Worldwide Search): Pre-calibrated for Lucknow (India), Lovelock, Nevada (USA), and Machakos (Kenya), while allowing users to click "Live GPS" or search any village worldwide to fetch live NASA POWER climate data and see 9 km (SMAP), 70 m (ECOSTRESS), and 10 m (Sentinel-2) sensor footprints on the map.

2. Benefits & Quantified Farmer Wealth Impact
Farming decisions come down to household economics. In our Lucknow benchmark, shifting from puddled Rice-Wheat-Bare Fallow (Rs 82,000/ha net return) to Option B (Direct-Seeded Rice/Maize -> Chickpea -> 60-Day Summer Moong) cuts irrigation water use by 44% to 48%, fixes +45 to +70 kg N/ha naturally in the soil (saving 2 bags of synthetic Urea per hectare), and adds +Rs 58,000/ha from the 60-day summer Moong harvest. Combined with Rs 11,200/ha saved in Urea and diesel, net farm income rises by +81% to Rs 1,48,500/ha.

3. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used
- Frontend & Geospatial UI: HTML5, CSS3, TailwindCSS, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), and Leaflet.js for interactive satellite footprint overlays.
- Agronomic & Critic Math Engine: Deterministic JavaScript equations implementing FAO-56 Penman-Monteith crop water deficits, soil-texture Available Water Capacity multipliers (0.65x for sandy, 1.0x for loam, 1.25x for clay), legume nitrogen credit models, and a 4-Agent verification pipeline (#BACKEND mode) comparing historical crop frequency against biophysical rules.
- Voice, Audio & Computer Vision: Browser Web Speech API (speechSynthesis and webkitSpeechRecognition supporting Devanagari Hindi, Hinglish, and English), Web Audio API (dual-frequency phone ringback and DTMF keypad tones), and HTML5 Canvas RGB pixel luminance analysis.
- Live APIs & Hosting: NASA POWER Agroclimatology REST API, Open-Meteo 5-Day Weather & ET0 API, OpenStreetMap Nominatim Geocoding API, and Netlify hosting.

4. Creativity & Human-in-the-Loop Considerations
Our proudest design choice is our refusal to blindly trust either satellite pixels or AI chatbots. For example, when water availability drops below 20% in summer, our Ruthless Critic (Agent 3) actively rejects planting ANY live summer cover crop because live plants would transpire the last remaining moisture needed for the June monsoon crop; instead, it recommends zero-water wheat stubble mulching. We also make sure farmers know that crop photos and satellite reflectance are screening aids, never a replacement for a real KVK or extension lab soil test.
